stem: Why is saving described as a leakage from the circular flow?

stem: Which is a limitation of the simple circular flow model?

options.content: It shows that income, output and expenditure are all different amounts
options.rationale: In the model these are equal.

options.content: It allows only households to take any economic decisions
options.rationale: Firms, the government and foreign sector also act.

options.content: It does not explain why injections and leakages change
options.rationale: Correct: it describes flows but not the causes of changes.

options.content: It requires an economy to have no trade with other countries
options.rationale: The open-economy version includes trade.

explanation: The model is descriptive; it does not give the causes of changes in spending, saving or investment, nor prices.

stem: Distinguish between an injection and a leakage.

points.description: An injection is an addition to the circular flow of income from outside the household–firm spending loop (investment, government spending, exports).
A leakage is income taken out of the flow that is not spent on domestically produced goods (saving, taxes, imports).

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: An injection is an addition to the circular flow, such as investment, government spending and exports. A leakage is income withdrawn from the flow and not spent on domestic output, such as saving, taxes and imports.

explanation: One mark for each.

stem: Explain what happens to national income if planned leakages exceed planned injections.

points.description: Spending on domestic output is less than the value of output produced.
Firms find that some output is unsold and stocks build up.
Firms cut output and employment.
National income falls until leakages equal injections at a new, lower equilibrium.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: If planned leakages exceed injections, spending on domestic output is less than the value of the output produced. Firms find that some goods are unsold and stocks build up, so they cut output and employment. National income falls until leakages equal injections at a new, lower equilibrium.

explanation: Spending below output, unsold stock, output cut, new equilibrium.
hints: Compare injections with leakages, then trace what firms do.

stem: Analyse how an increase in government spending on roads, financed by borrowing, would affect national income in the circular flow.

points.description: Government spending is an injection, so injections rise above leakages.
Construction firms receive more revenue and hire more workers (higher factor incomes).
Households spend part of the extra income, creating further rounds of spending.
Part of the extra income leaks into saving, taxes and imports, so the effect gradually dies away.
National income rises until leakages again equal the higher injections.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Government spending is an injection, so injections rise above leakages. Construction firms receive more revenue and hire more workers, so factor incomes rise. Households spend part of the extra income, creating further rounds of spending. Part of the extra income leaks into saving, taxes and imports, so each round is smaller. National income rises until leakages again equal the higher level of injections.

explanation: Injection up, incomes up, further spending, leakages, new equilibrium.
hints: Trace the effect of a rise in government spending around the flow.

stem: Assess the importance of the international sector for the level of national income in a small open economy.

points.description: Exports are an injection, so changes in foreign demand change income.
Imports are a leakage, so a high import share reduces the effect of any injection on domestic income.
A small economy with a large trade share is exposed to external shocks (world prices, demand).
Export earnings can also fund imports of capital goods that raise future income.
Trade lets the economy specialise, which increases output and income.
Other factors (government spending, investment, saving) also affect income.
The importance depends on the share of trade in national income and the diversity of exports.
A justified conclusion.

levels.descriptor: Two-sided, applied and developed, with a justified conclusion.
Some development of one or both sides, limited application or conclusion.

answerSpec.modelAnswer: In a small open economy exports are a large injection, so changes in foreign demand and world prices can change national income substantially, and a high share of imports is a large leakage which reduces the effect of any injection on domestic income. The economy is therefore exposed to external shocks, especially if it depends on one or two exports. However, trade also lets the economy specialise, and export earnings pay for imports of machinery and fuel that raise future income. Domestic investment, government spending and saving also matter. Overall the international sector is very important in a small economy with a large trade share, though its effect depends on how diversified its exports are and on domestic policy.

explanation: Weigh the exposure to external shocks against the gains from trade.
hints: Consider how trade changes the injections and leakages.
